core_obligations: The logarithmic expansion at proof lines 238-241: log F_{a,c}(zeta;q) is written as a double sum and the geometric series in q^{ck} is summed in closed form, giving minus the sum over k of zeta^k q^{ak} divided by k(1 - q^{ck}).

The splitting of the index at proof lines 242-253: writing k = m b + j and substituting q = exp(-z) turns the sum into a Riemann sum of the auxiliary function f, whose Taylor expansion at the origin is stated at proof line 254.

The application of Lemma lemma11 at proof lines 255-259: the expansion of f produces the pole term in 1/z together with the logarithmic term carrying psi(j/b), and the remaining terms are collected into O(|z|).

The two root-of-unity sums at proof lines 260-268: the digamma identity evaluates one sum and the zeta-value identity evaluates the other, so that the orthogonality relation sum of zeta^j = 0 kills the constant term.
Exponentiation at proof lines 269-272: exponentiating the collected logarithm produces exactly the displayed asymptotic formula, so the proof ends with the asserted statement.
proof_roadmap: Take the logarithm of the q-Pochhammer product defining F_{a,c} and sum the resulting geometric series in q^{ck}.
Replace the index k by m b + j and recognise the inner sum as a Riemann sum of the auxiliary function f.
Apply the Taylor expansion of f at the origin, with the zeta-value term supplied by the article's Lemma lemma11.
Evaluate the two root-of-unity sums with the digamma identity and orthogonality, then exponentiate.
